items.title: Bridging Policy and Practice: Recommendations for Parental Support in Plastic Surgery
items.summary: Pregnancy, parental leave, and lactation remain challenging for surgical trainees, yet specialty-specific data in plastic and reconstructive surgery (PRS) are limited.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: High-risk cosmetic procedures: what crackdown means for nurses
items.summary: Leading cosmetic nurses have welcomed proposals from the government to “crack down on cosmetic cowboys” by introducing new restrictions on who can perform high-risk procedures.
items.source: Nursing Times

items.title: Government sets out detail of crackdown on cosmetic procedures
items.summary: The Government has set out proposals for limiting who can carry out high-risk cosmetic procedures such as liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), vampire facials and chemical peels.
items.source: Pulse Today

items.title: Robot-assisted (super) microsurgery: a randomized in vivo preclinical trial for microvascular anastomosis
items.summary: Microsurgery's requirement for extraordinary surgical skill, physical endurance, and prolonged training impedes widespread clinical implementation. This study evaluated objective histological metrics and subjective parameters of a multi-modular microsurgical robotic system in a rat model.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Exceptional Referral Protocol: Primary Vetting Outcomes in the East of Scotland Following the Introduction of Clinical Photography.
items.summary: The NHS Scotland Exceptional Referral Protocol (ERP), recently renamed the National Referral Protocol (NRP)(SGHD CMO (2025) 17), provides a pathway for patients seeking body-altering procedures where there is an aesthetic element.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Which Motor Branch to Use? Targeted Muscle Reinnervation for Digital Neuromas: An Anatomical Study
items.summary: Symptomatic neuromas following digital nerve injury frequently cause persistent pain and impaired hand function.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: “Long-term results of 149 free fibula flap reconstructions in extensive limb defects: Experiences from nine European hospitals”
items.summary: Dear Editors…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: “Management of severe post-burn deformities of the hand.”
items.summary: To the Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: Complications and health costs of cosmetic tourism. A systematic review
items.summary: Dear Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Quality of life after mastectomy alone compared with subpectoral breast reconstruction using the BREAST-Q and RAND-36
items.summary: Mastectomy can negatively affect health-related quality of life (HR-QoL). Subpectoral breast reconstruction can be performed to restore breast contour and may improve HR-QoL. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term impact of mastectomy alone compared with subpectoral breast reconstruction.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: “Advancing Gender-Affirming Surgery Medicare Policies in Canada: A Qualitative Description Study”
items.summary: Gender-affirming surgery (GAS) is one component of gender-affirming care. Access to GAS in Canada remains inconsistent due to jurisdictional differences in GAS policies.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Quantitative Analysis of Tissue Oxygenation Trajectories in DIEP Flaps Using Near Infrared Spectroscopy – A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.summary: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is an adjunct for monitoring breast free flaps. There is a paucity of studies using large NIRS datasets to characterize how patient-, flap-, and operative-level factors and systemic hemodynamics influence postoperative StO₂.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Unilateral Macrostomia Repair with Modified Muscle Reconstruction: Long-term Anthropometric Evaluation of Static and Smile Symmetry
items.summary: Macrostomia, or transverse facial cleft, significantly impairs facial aesthetics and oral function. While various repair techniques have been reported, achieving satisfactory bilateral symmetry, particularly during dynamic expressions such as smiling, remains a challenge.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Impact of diabetes mellitus on clinical outcome in burns patients managed in a national burns centre
items.summary: The impact of diabetes mellitus on outcomes following burn injury remains unclear. This study aimed to characterise diabetic burn patients and their outcomes at a national burns centre.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: The use of preoperative CTA and MRA for DIEP flap breast reconstruction: a 15-year multicentre retrospective analysis
items.summary: This study aimed to evaluate the benefits of preoperative Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) versus Magnetic Resonance Angiography (MRA) for surgical outcomes in deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flap breast reconstruction, compared with patients without preoperative imaging.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Palatal Microcirculation in Minimal-Incision Cleft Palate Repair: Impact of Lateral Releasing Incisions — A Controlled Intraoperative Studyṅ
items.summary: Tissue perfusion is critical for wound healing after cleft palate repair. Many palatoplasty techniques incorporate lateral releasing incisions for tissue mobilization, yet their impact on palatal microcirculation remains unclear.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Impact of a Neck Exoskeleton Device on Plastic Surgery Resident Ergonomics
items.summary: Plastic surgery residents are at high risk for work-related musculoskeletal discomfort. We hypothesize that resident postural ergonomics are poor and may improve with a passive exoskeleton device.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Establishment and validation of a nomogram for predicting pain relief after nerve deactivation surgery in refractory migraine
items.summary: To explore the influencing factors of symptom relief in patients after nerve deactivation surgery for refractory migraine, establish a symptom relief prediction model, and verify its accuracy.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Unexpected Admissions After Planned Outpatient Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer Reconstruction: Risk Factors and a Bedside Risk Score
items.summary: Non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC) reconstruction is overwhelmingly performed as outpatient surgery, yet a subset of patients scheduled for same-day discharge require unplanned admission or prolonged observation. No procedure-specific preoperative risk tool currently exists.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Commentary to: Nationwide trends in breast reconstruction in Korea during the reimbursement era (2015–2023)
items.summary: The nationwide analysis by Jeon and colleagues provides an important perspective on how breast reconstruction has evolved within a changing healthcare environment.1 Using national claims data from 2015 to 2023, the authors demonstrate a substantial increase in breast reconstruction relative to mastectomy procedures…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Effect of neoadjuvant chemotherapy on surgical outcomes in Danish breast cancer patients between 2018-2023
items.summary: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) has been used nationwide in Denmark to downsize tumour and for downstaging of metastases in the axilla. Although several studies have assessed the impact of NACT on surgical complications after immediate breast reconstruction (IBR), the available evidence remains inconsistent.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: DIEP versus SIEA flap in autologous breast reconstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: While the deep inferior epigastric artery perforator (DIEP) flap is regarded as the gold standard in autologous breast reconstruction (ABR), the superficial inferior epigastric artery (SIEA) flap has been proposed as a muscle- and fascia-sparing alternative.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Chemotherapy and microsurgical-related vascular complications in DIEP Flap Breast Reconstruction: A Retrospective Study
items.summary: To evaluate the association between preoperative chemotherapy and microsurgical vascular complications in patients undergoing Deep Inferior Epigastric Perforator (DIEP) flap breast reconstruction, and whether chemotherapy timing affects risk.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Comparison of Palmaris Longus and Split Flexor Carpi Radialis Tendon Grafts in Two-Stage Flexor Tendon Reconstruction
items.summary: Two-stage flexor tendon reconstruction remains an important option for delayed or missed Zone II flexor tendon injuries when direct repair is no longer feasible. Although the palmaris longus is commonly used as a donor tendon, it may be absent, unavailable, or unsuitable in some patients.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Beyond the chatbot: AI-assisted software development for plastic surgeons
items.summary: Dear Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Staged Arteriovenous Loops: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 84 Patients
items.summary: Arteriovenous loops (AVLs) are widely used as an alternative to vein grafts in free flap reconstruction. While single-stage AVLs are well established, the safety profile and clinical implications of staged AVLs remain incompletely defined.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Correspondence on: Decreased need for botulinum toxin and nerve blocks after headache surgery
items.summary: Dear Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Unexpected Returns to the Operating Room after Microsurgical Breast Reconstruction – A qualitative Study of Patients’ Experiences
items.summary: Unplanned takebacks after microsurgical breast reconstruction are rare but potentially distressing events.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Postoperative complication risks associated with penicillin allergy in tissue expander-based breast reconstruction: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study
items.summary: Reported penicillin allergy often leads to avoidance of first-line β-lactam prophylaxis in favor of less effective alternatives, potentially increasing surgical site infection (SSI) risk. Tissue expander (TE)–based breast reconstruction, despite being a clean procedure, has infection rates of up to 30%.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Snookered by the Bilobed Flap: A Simple Visual Geometric Aid for Zitelli Bilobed Flap Design
items.summary: The bilobed flap is a versatile method of facial reconstruction, particularly for small defects of the lower third of the nose.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Thirty-Day Outcomes After Pediatric Microtia and Anotia Reconstruction: A CPT-Coded National Cohort Study
items.summary: Microtia reconstruction requires balancing short-term safety, operative burden, staging, donor-site morbidity, aesthetic goals, hearing needs, and long-term revision risk. National data describing early postoperative outcomes across CPT-defined reconstructive phenotypes remain limited.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: A Last Resort that Works: Distal Deep Vein Arterialization in No-Option Diabetic Critical Limb Threatening Ischemia: A Prospective Interventional Study
items.summary: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is the most advanced stage of peripheral arterial disease, characterized by ischemic rest pain, non-healing ulcers, and gangrene. In patients with “no-option” CLTI, distal deep vein arterialization (DDVA) offers a potential limb salvage strategy.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Expander-Phase Morbidity in RFID-Enabled Two-Stage Breast Reconstruction: A Multicenter Risk Prediction Model and Clinical Nomogram
items.summary: Two-stage implant-based breast reconstruction (TSBR) using tissue expanders (TE) remains a standard procedure.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Comparing Resident Self-Assessment and Faculty Assessment in Plastic Surgery Training: A Simulation-Based Study
items.summary: Self-assessment is a valuable component of surgical training, allowing trainees to identify areas for improvement and direct future learning.1 Under the Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills (OSATS) framework, technical performance can be assessed using complementary instruments.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Perioperative GLP-1 Analog Management in Abdominoplasty: A Multicenter Comparative Study of Cessation and Resumption Timing on Weight Outcomes and Complications
items.summary: The increasing use of GLP-1 receptor agonists for weight loss has created a growing population of patients seeking abdominoplasty, yet evidence-based guidelines for perioperative management of these medications remain lacking.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Supraclavicular Artery Island Flap for Head and Neck Reconstruction: Our Experience and Exploratory Analysis of Risk Factors
items.summary: The supraclavicular artery island flap (SCAIF) is increasingly being utilized for reconstruction of complex head and neck defects as an alternative to the traditional free flap or pedicled pectoralis flap.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Effectiveness of Upper Extremity Lymphaticovenular Anastomosis for Breast Cancer-Related Trunk Lymphedema: Evaluating with a Novel Subjective Scoring System
items.summary: Secondary trunk lymphedema (TL) commonly develops after breast cancer treatment (BCT) and frequently exists with upper extremity lymphedema (UEL). Although several diagnostic methods have been proposed, treatment options are limited mainly to manual lymphatic drainage (MLD).
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Plastic Surgery Access Deserts in the United States: A GIS-Based National Assessment
items.summary: Timely access to plastic and reconstructive surgery is critical for trauma, burns, congenital anomalies, hand conditions, and oncologic reconstruction. Prior workforce studies often rely on county- or state-level surgeon counts, which fail to capture patient travel burden.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Postoperative complications after abdominal wall reconstruction using anterolateral thigh and tensor fasciae latae flaps: a retrospective comparative cohort study
items.summary: The anterolateral thigh (ALT) and tensor fasciae latae (TFL) flaps are useful options for autologous abdominal wall reconstruction. However, direct comparisons of postoperative outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to compare postoperative complications between these two flap types.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial of Three Different Types of Webspace Reconstruction for Congenital Syndactyly Release
items.summary: Release of syndactyly includes the use of full-thickness skin grafts or graftless techniques with specially designed flaps. Recently, artificial dermal substitutes have been reported to be successfully used for web reconstruction without skin grafting.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.summary: Dear Editor…
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery

items.title: Do body contouring surgical procedures improve medical disorders and quality of life?
items.summary: Patients undergoing body contouring surgery often present with medical symptoms resulting from weight loss or pregnancy. The change in quality of life resulting from treatment of these symptoms warrants further investigation to help fully communicate this potential benefit to patients considering aesthetic surgery.
items.source: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery
